hits.draft_en:
One of the biggest posts on my feed today reckons open-plan kitchens will be gone from most homes in 10 or 20 years.

If you flip houses, that's worth a thought. The wall you knock out this year is the layout you're selling in two.

Before you swing the hammer, run it both ways. In FlipPro you paste an Aussie listing URL, then compare feasibility scenarios with the reno quotes kept separate from the purchase price.
hits.video_tip: 20-30s screen recording on flippro.ai: paste a real public listing URL, open Feasibility and flick between two scenarios. Narrate one line per screen. Only show screens the FlipPro bot confirms are live.

hits.draft_en:
Thinking of moving every server from Ubuntu to Debian this week?

Before the first one moves, write down how you'd move it back.

Nearly 30 years in disaster recovery has taught me that a migration without a rollback plan is a gamble. Take a snapshot, keep the old box running until the new one has had a full week of real traffic, and test the restore, not only the backup.
hits.video_tip: 20-30s screen recording on a throwaway test VM: take a snapshot, run the upgrade, then roll back from the snapshot. Caption 'write down how you'd move it back' over the rollback. No client systems on screen.

Nobody running a small business wants "AI powered".

They want the quotes out the same day. The inbox sorted before they sit down. This month's supplier prices checked against last month's.

So at Gee IT we start every AI job with one question: which hour of your week do you want back? Then we build the agent for that.

narrative_synthesis: levelsio carried Monday with 16 of the 23 hits: a private jet crash explained as odds per trip (1,636,149 views), a bold call that open-plan kitchens will disappear (196,407), a passkeys take (195,645) and the Battlefield 1942 browser port built with Claude Code (188,263, then 68,996 for the playable launch). Security and outages kept pulling bookmarks, with Ubuntu's unpatched hole and a possible move to Debian (112,429) and Cloudflare Email Sending down for 12 hours (110,133). Greg Isenberg's 'Grok Bots for boring SMBs' plan pulled 1,157 bookmarks, and his 'nobody wants AI powered' copywriting take drew 220 replies. Tony Dinh and levelsio both argued agents don't need MCPs. Nobody on the watchlist talked about rollback plans for a big migration, or what small businesses want from AI in plain terms. Those are Nick's lanes.
